title: Tarkov Companion paired-device protocol 2.0
$comment: String limits are UTF-8 byte limits enforced by CompanionProtocolJson; maxLength is an additional character bound. Object property order is not significant, including the position of polymorphic 'type' discriminators. Unknown optional object fields remain readable within negotiated major 2; unknown discriminators and enum members fail closed. Constructor invariants that JSON Schema cannot express (thumbprints, signatures, transcript hashes, revision/change-id rules, lifetimes, and canonical chunking) are normative in docs/PAIRED_DEVICE_PROTOCOL.md and enforced by the C# boundary.

timeSpan.$comment: A control lease duration: whole milliseconds, positive, at most five minutes (enforced by the C# boundary).

ephemeralPublicKey.$comment: An uncompressed P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo of exactly 91 bytes.

originDeepLink.$comment: A companion deep link only; the desktop never passes it to the operating-system shell.

commandAcknowledgement.$comment: Only Applied names this command as the applied change. Stale, conflict, preview, and snapshot responses carry canonical state describing the aggregate cursor; every other rejection describes no revision (zero and null).

ciphertextLength.$comment: u16(payload kind) followed by the 1-65536 byte JSON root.

ciphertextChunksBase64Url.$comment: base64url(ciphertext) cut into 1024-character chunks; only the last may be shorter.

pairingNonceReveal.$comment: A handshake challenge also names the attempt and desktop nonce, so the root oneOf excludes it here.

v2ContractVersion.$comment: Core V2ContractVersion; its read-only isDefined member is written and ignored on read.

workspaceOrigin.$comment: Core WorkspaceOrigin: audit attribution, not authentication.

pairedScanIntent.$comment: Core ScanIntent without Flea, which is never a paired capture intent.

captureIntentState.$comment: Core CaptureIntentState; a paired intent always expires, at most two minutes after it was armed.

mapMarkState.$comment: Core MapMarkState: the user's own annotation in map plane coordinates, never a player position. Labels are at most 80 UTF-16 code units.
